title: Autoscaler warmup-starvation after heterogeneous instance rebalance leads to reserved-pool shortfall and customer throttles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers experienced sustained 429/503 errors and elevated tail latency during two evening traffic spikes after a control-plane rolling rebalance across heterogeneous GPU host types. Symptoms: requests hit burst limits and were throttled even though reserved-pool metrics reported nominal capacity. Impact: three customers reported production degradations and opened escalations; one requested credits for a 12-hour window of degraded throughput.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-12 18:40 UTC first customer alert; 18:47 paging triggered; 18:50 on-call confirmed spikes and 429s. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler failed to spawn warm workers fast enough. Telemetry: reserved-pool headroom dropped sharply while pool instance count stayed flat. We observed a repeated pattern after a control-plane rebalance that moved tenants between hot/cold racks with different GPU families. Logs: scale-controller accepted warmup-complete events from node-agent earlier than the agent had finished GPU kernel compilation on new hosts. Correlation: hosts with older driver + new model quantization path were slower to compile kernels, but the agent emitted a readiness flag due to a regression in the warmup acknowledgement path.
root_cause: A race in scale-controller warmup acknowledgment logic combined with an optimistic readiness signal from the node-agent caused the controller to mark new nodes as 'warmed' prematurely. The autoscaler then relied on the inflated warm capacity when computing burst headroom, allowing burst accounting to be consumed without actual warm slots available. The issue was triggered by heterogeneous host types (different GPU drivers/kernels) exposed by a rolling rebalance; an optimization introduced in dedicated-2026.02 skipped an explicit kernel-compile completion check under certain paths.
mitigation: 1) Immediate revert of the optimistic warmup-path optimization (hotfix deployed 2026-03-13 03:15 UTC). 2) Emergency patch to scale-controller to treat warmup-acknowledged nodes as soft-ready until a readiness probe confirms GPU kernel readiness (deployed 2026-03-13 04:10 UTC). 3) Temporarily raised burst safety floor for affected tenants to avoid further throttles while patch propagates. 4) Customer comms sent with mitigation summary and offer for credits; one customer accepted credit offer.
rollback_and_hotfix_instructions: Hotfix deploy: revert commit 0f3a9b4 (warmup-optim) and roll scale-controller change with feature-flag disabled by default. Steps: 1) cherry-pick revert to release branch, 2) run canary in us-west-2 with synthetic warmup tests, 3) promote across regions with 5-minute pause between regions, 4) monitor reserved-pool headroom and 99.9th latency. Rollback: if errors increase, toggle feature-flag and revert to prior control-plane state using traffic switch.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (immediate): hotfix to mark warm nodes as soft-ready and increase burst floor for impacted clusters (complete). Phase 2 (1 week): add explicit kernel-compile readiness probe in node-agent and update warmup handshake. Phase 3 (2 weeks): run mixed-instance chaos testing for rebalances, add telemetry guardrails for optimistic-ack counts. Phase 4 (30 days): add quota reconciliation job to repair any burst-ledger imbalances caused during the incident.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No customer throttles attributable to warmup-race during two synthetic rebalance tests across heterogeneous hosts. 2) Reserved-pool headroom metrics accurately reflect warm-ready slot count for 24 hours. 3) Post-deploy regression window (48h) shows <1% error-rate increase and burst accounting stable. 4) Updated runbook and customer-facing postmortem drafted and reviewed.
postmortem_actions: Add explicit kernel readiness probe to node-agent and surface compile metrics
Backfill and reconcile burst-ledger for affected tenants and issue credits where required
Introduce a telemetry alarm for optimistic warmup-ack spikes during rebalances
Expand warmup integration tests to include heterogeneous-driver hosts
Schedule tabletop run with SRE, Autoscale, and Agent teams to practice rolling rebalance recovery
